# The ML's Last Stand (#31) — one month, pre-registered, then the question closes

*Auto-generated by `lab/last_stand.py`. ⚠️ **EDUCATIONAL SIMULATION** — nothing here is advice, and the universe is survivorship-biased, so every number is DIRECTIONAL.*

## The criterion, fixed before any arm ran

> A challenger earns the product engine **only** by beating 12-1 momentum on the long-only top-20 book under the #27 duel rules — after-cost Sharpe **AND** a consistent Rank IC advantage (a majority of calendar years). **Anything less: momentum keeps the engine, permanently.**

"Consistent" is fixed as beating momentum's Rank IC in more than 50% of calendar years. Applied as arithmetic by `signal_duel.decide()`, not as a judgement after the fact.

---

## Arm 1 — v2 clean LGBM (A-1 fixed)

**The one change.** `size` was `log(adj_close)`: a retroactively re-written series, so its value at a past date moved whenever a later split or dividend landed (#25 finding **A-1**). It is now `log(close)` — the price that actually traded that day, never rewritten. Raw close was chosen over point-in-time market cap deliberately: it keeps v2 a **one-variable** change from v1, which is what makes this rematch attributable. Architecture, hyperparameters, feature list, label, walk-forward schedule and 21-day embargo are all unchanged.

The shipped v1 model and its stored predictions were **not touched** — they are the historical record. v2 writes to its own `*_v2` artifacts, and the build asserts v1's feature table mtime is unchanged before it exits.

### Result — 47 walk-forward OOS months, 2022-06-15 → 2026-04-23

| Book | n | Ann. return | Ann. vol | Sharpe | Sortino | MaxDD | Mean Rank IC | t |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A · Momentum (12-1) *(control)* | 47 | +23.93% | +12.51% | 1.792 | 3.317 | -12.03% | 0.0414 | 1.58 |
| B · v1 ML (A-1 contaminated) | 47 | +20.62% | +14.14% | 1.407 | 2.436 | -15.20% | 0.0505 | 1.64 |
| B · v2 ML (A-1 fixed) | 47 | +21.47% | +14.23% | 1.448 | 2.662 | -14.70% | 0.0492 | 1.61 |

| Book | Mean monthly turnover |
|---|---|
| A · Momentum (12-1) | +47.88% |
| B · v1 ML (A-1 contaminated) | +29.99% |
| B · v2 ML (A-1 fixed) | +28.95% |

### Verdict — momentum keeps the engine

* After-cost Sharpe: momentum **1.792** vs v2 **1.448** → challenger wins on Sharpe: **NO**
* Rank IC consistency: v2 beat momentum in **2 of 5** years (40%) → consistent: **NO**
* **Earns the product engine: NO**

### The finding: A-1 was never carrying the ML

This is the arm that was supposed to give the ML its fairest possible shot, and the honest headline is how **little** the fix changed:

| | v1 (contaminated) | v2 (clean) | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| After-cost Sharpe | 1.407 | 1.448 | +0.041 |
| Mean Rank IC | 0.0505 | 0.0492 | -0.0013 |
| Turnover | +29.99% | +28.95% | |

Rank IC moved **down** slightly on the clean feature, which is the direction a removed leak should move it — the contamination was worth a sliver of spurious ranking skill. Sharpe moved *up* slightly. Both moves are far smaller than the gap to momentum, and neither changes any verdict.

**This closes the asymmetric ruling, and it closes it cleanly.** #28 fixed the reading in advance: *ML loses ⇒ conclusive; ML wins ⇒ inconclusive pending a clean retrain.* The #30 duel was an ML loss, so it was already conclusive — but the caveat "a clean model might do better" remained technically open. It is now closed by measurement rather than by argument: **the clean model does not do better in any way that matters.** No contamination caveat survives on this question.

Worth stating plainly because it cuts against my own earlier framing: the asymmetric ruling was the right discipline, and the thing it was guarding against turned out not to exist. That is what a correctly-specified control looks like when it comes back negative.

### Consequences already applied

* `size` is fixed in `utils/sp500_features.py` — the leak is closed for every future build, not just for v2.

* The two A-1 tripwire tests **flipped as designed** and have been rewritten to assert the fixed behaviour, plus a third that checks `size` still *responds* to the raw price actually changing (a test that only asserts immobility would also pass if the feature were a constant).

* Fixing A-1 exposed a flaw in the test fixture itself: `close` and `adj_close` were identical in the synthetic panel, so one of the two tripwires had been passing **vacuously** — it could never have detected the change it existed to detect. The fixture now makes them differ.

## Closure statement · *pending arms 2 and 3*

Arm 1 verdict: **momentum keeps the engine.** The clean v2 model loses on after-cost Sharpe (1.448 vs 1.792) and fails the consistency clause (40% of years). Under the pre-stated criterion that is not a marginal result to be revisited — it is the answer the criterion was written to produce.
